You won’t have enough time to see everything but definitely use the audio guide. You will be blown away by its awesomeness. Our 16 year old son picked this as his favorite day during our entire European vacation.

Stonehenge was next and I loved it. While it was crowded, you could still get some great pictures and selfies. You can take the bus or walk to it. We walked back to the bus and bought some fresh berries and honey from a local vendor. You won’t need much time but I do recommend you walk around it because you do get different views and a different perspective as you walk around. It was more impressive than I imagined!!

Roman baths were next and while it was my least favorite, it was still OK and I’m glad we experienced it. We bought tickets to go through and it was a waste of money, in my opinion. It’s a nice area to walk around and get ice cream or a quick snack. Architecture is amazing and it’s quaint. We went through the Basilica and it was impressive. We had to wait until mass was over so try to see it before mass if possible.

Dinner at Red Lion Inn was awesome! See my review on that. Sam took our order on the bus which enabled us to get our food and drinks shortly after we arrived. Keep in mind you need to purchase your alcoholic drinks or sodas. There is a vegetarian option and a good variety of meals to choose from. Four options in total, including fish and chips which was a family favorite.

Only negative is that where Premium Tours is located (3 Gates, I believe!) it’s super crowded and there is not a lot of organization. It’s not always clear where to be. There are monitors with tours and times they are leaving, but it’s confusing and people are stupid when all crowded together...LOL. Just leave time to get there early (not more than 30 minutes). Plenty of places to grab a bite for breakfast but there will be lines.

The tour results were more than I expected, and it turned out just as described. The coach was new. They got us to Windsor Castle early enough to get in queue before the large crowds arrived. Our guide, Steve Maynard was very organized and made sure we all got the most time possible at each stop. Steve was extremely knowledgeable, informative and witty. He kept the entire trip enjoyable :) Steve can also suggest where to eat and what to do in London. Our driver Bradley E. got us everywhere quickly, safely and avoided traffic as much as possible. Get to the station 45 minutes early to use the toilet and to get something to eat. They don't sell or serve refreshments on the bus and the bus doesn't have a toilet. People brought snacks and drinks on board. There were places to purchase drinks and snacks at every stop. Surprisingly the A/C on the only had on or cold. Bring a light jacket for the ride. You can safely leave your belongings on the coach. Even though it is stressed to return on time some people don't and that eats away time from your next stop. Don't be those people!

This tour was easily the most instagram worthy tour of our trip. I LOVED IT. The Royal Wedding is coming up in May, so make sure you see the Royal Apartments and Knight's rooms so you can say you've been there! My favorite part was BAth, but that was the primary reason we booked this trip to begin with. As a Harry Potter fan, I WAS SO SHOCKED TO VISIT THE REAL GODRIC'S HOLLOW. That was an awesome surpise. The pub was so cute and delicious, you could feel it's history as soon as you walked through the front door.

Easily the best part of my England trip. 10/10 do recommend.

I understand why the tour guide would combine these 3 historic sites as they are located in relatively close proximity - west of London a couple of hours. Windsor Castle was so fascinating and filled with hundreds of years of history! It's definitely what one thinks a castle would look like, and it did not disappoint. We arrived before it opened so we wouldn't have much of a wait. The tour is self-guided with Hand-held audio recordings. Unfortunately, we were required to return to the bus in such a short time that we had to breeze through many of the rooms, and didn't even get the chance to see St. George's Chapel whih I was told was a must-see. Our tour guide was David and he was wonderful, teaching us about England's history and about the sites we were about to see. So by the time we got to Stonehenge we didn't need to read the placards around the stones. We spent more time at Stonehenge than at Windsor, it seemed. By 3:30 p.m. we finally arrived for lunch at The George Inn in Lacock, a quaint pub with good food. It was so much later than I wanted to wait for lunch. By the time we arrived in Bath it was 4:55, and we literally RAN to the Roman Baths to get in before their last admittance at 5:00 p.m. Because we arrived so late, we didn't get to see the Bath Cathedral, and had very limited time at the Roman Baths. I would have preferred to see only Windsor Castle and Bath, but that was not offered as a tour. I would not recommend this particular tour for the above reasons. But if you're fine not seeing much of any one place, this may be good for you.

This was truly a "taste of ..." tour. Our guide, Steven Maynard was as excellent as you could want. He did explain in the very beginning that it was a taste of all four places but you should know that before you consider whether that's what you want to sign up for or not. It's a long day because it's a lot of driving in the bus. These places aren't central London. You'll meet at the bus around 7:30am and we got back around 9pm. Still, we only had about an hour at each place to roam around. For me, I would have liked more time at Windsor Castle, Bath was OK but too many people and would have been OK skipping. We had lunch at Lacock and would have liked more time wondering around that town. A very cool 14th century village. We had about an hour at Stonehenge and that was actually just about right for me.
I did enjoy it. One thing I'd ask Premium Tours to consider is to limit it to maybe 5 years old an older. One very nice couple had 17 month old twins. At least one was crying all the time. All that time in their laps in the bus? Can't imagine infants liking that. It made the trip painful for everyone around them. They felt bad, but I don't think they should have done this one with the two infants.

We took the tour of Windsor Castle, Stonehenge and Bath, with lunch at a pub in Lacock. The tour guide was friendly and provided many facts throughout the coach bus ride. She gave us a lot of information while on the bus, but once off the bus, we were left on our own. Our tour group was quite large, probably over 35 people.

The first issue I had was that we weren’t given headsets to hear the guide once we were off the bus and walking to our destination. A headset is pretty standard in every group tour I have taken. This tour didn’t have this, instead, the guide spoke into a mini mic and you couldn’t hear her if you were at the back of the line. Another time, while waiting on line to see Windsor castle, she has to say everything 3 times so everyone could hear her instructions.

The second issue I had was that our guide didn’t “guide” us. At both Windsor and Stonehenge, we were given an electronic prerecorded handheld device that guided us around. The tour guide didn’t lead us around, we were basically on our own. We were given a set time to meet back at the bus, and told to take the prerecorded tours.

Next, our lunch at the pub was pretty disappointing. The food wasn’t very good. Also, no drinks were included! We had to pay an additional £3 per person for a soda!

Finally, the Bath “tour” wasn’t a tour. Again, we were given a time to return and then set free to roam around. The bath house, wasn’t even included in the price of this tour. It was an additional £17 per person to enter.

I wouldn’t recommend this company. Look for a company that has a guide lead you around, instead of having you listen to prerecorded tours, which were provided free of charge by the site.

My daughter and I took the tour. We arrived very early at the bus station (7:15) so as to find the right bus. The coach was a double-decker and we elected to ride on the top. I sometimes suffer a little from motion sickness, but the driver was very smooth. We would never have seen the country-side had we not taken this tour. Our guide (Steve?) was very knowledgable and interesting (even funny.) We saw Windsor, where we were advised to grab a sandwich, because the pub lunch was to be at 3:00. We are glad we did! We next went to Stonehenge, which was awe-inspriring. I learned a lot about the history. We next went to Lacock,, a cute English village, for lunch, which was disappointing. The village was quite picturesque. We ended up at Bath. We enjoyed seeing the church there, but felt we could have left this part out of our trip. It was a tiring day, but definitely worth it.

This tour covered a lot of ground in one day so I appreciated the timely schedule. Guide Lucy was very funny and kept us in line so the tour was enjoyable for us all. Super comfy doubledecker bus for the day. Very happy I took this tour!

My husband and I went on this trip during our recent trip to London. While there is plenty to do and see in the city, we always want to get out and see the outside of city centers. But this is beyond "getting out of the city". The historical site is a must on any visit.! We had a great guide with Nick....he was knowledgable, witty and professional. He offered options along the way to join him for walking/talking tours that I highly recommend. The ride was long, but the beauty is there if you want to see all the parts of a country, not just the city. The lunch in the quaint town of Lacock was delicious, with excellent service. London has a lot to offer, but make sure you get outside the city to see what this lovely country has to offer..

Starting right on time to beat traffic and got to Windsor well ahead of any other tour group. Our guide, Lucy, like a drill sergeant made sure that we were the first at Windsor waiting for it to open. And we are glad for it. She was extremely knowledgeable and was commenting most of the way on the bus. Wish there was more time at Windsor, but with the day so packed, we realize that's all the time we have. On to Bath, it is a bit of a ride through some beautiful country side. Admission to the Bath museum is not included, but we were glad we went in - quite interesting.

Late lunch (3pm) at Lackok - George Inn, a quaint pub in a small village. It is amazing how well organized the staff were in serving a bus load of customers with whatever each one ordered. Now on to Stonehenge just in time before the last entry. We were free to visit. You can only walk around a perimeter setup, not a lot of time to explore surrounding area.

On our 2 hour ride back, Lucy helped us figure out the best drop off point to reach our hotels.

Overall, it was a very good trip and recommend it.

If you take the Stonehenge/Windsor Castle and Bath please take the tour that includes your lunch, otherwise you may be the only one that does not get to eat in the restaurant and for the difference in price most definitely worth it! I took this tour, left early and we arrived at Windsor Castle, a fast security check then onto the grounds of Windsor, Had a fantastic tour of the Castle, many rooms and lots of time did not feel rushed at all! I bought a few post cards with pictures of the rooms I saw because you can not take pictures inside the castle. Also got a few souvenirs. Not too expensive either. Then got back on the bus on our way to eat lunch. Enjoyed a relaxed lunch very English and got to know my fellow bus passengers from all over the world this was a treat! Otherwise you don't get to talk much on the bus. Then off to Stonehenge, the plus for us that day was that we had only sun. Not a cloud in the sky which is very rare as per our tour guide and because of this we got to see Stonehenge for a few seconds from the highway while still on the bus. We parked and got off. You can not see Stonehenge from the parking lot at all! You have to pass through the gift shop and then towards a tunnel and along these walls is a painted mural of the past thousands of years of how the stones were placed and of the different people/tribes that contributed to the creation. This wall is a true historical beauty! The walk around only takes about 2 minutes and once you are out and up from this tunnel, OMG my heart stops, there it is! Breathtaking to see it in person. Stonehenge finally. You walk around the stones, protected by a cord, because the stones have become too fragile. Took about 50 pictures of me standing at every 2 feet around to get every inch LOL. Glad we made it there by about 230pm before sundown which was at around 430p.Don't forget the gift shop! I bought a mini Stonehenge. Then we were off to Bath. The road to Bath and seeing the towns and the houses with grass roofs were a real treat! Once we arrived in Bath, another surprise, the Baths!! Many of them to visit in different rooms, also the biggest bath with no roof top, imagining how it was hundreds of years ago, when parliament met there for meetings, bringing along families and friends, enjoying the baths in the then clean water. Now the baths are no longer clean just for show but you can stand by them and put your hand in, take a picture of you there and imagine how it was, and even in the winter the water is very warm. Walked around Bath, visited shops, bought more souvenirs had free time until 8pm grabbed a potato sandwich which is very popular there, and ate it on the bus ride back to London. I wish so much to go back soon!!

Booked this tour and they canceled on me last minute very unprofessional, when you accepted a reservation you have an obligation to fulfill it, plans are made months in advance and this kind of behavior is not fair to someone who flew half way around the world to see Stonehenge regardless of the number of reservations you got

Bad service, very expensive.
No support whatsoever even from managers
Their only pourpose is to take the money without to provide any service at all.
The price, service and support the worst ever saw.

This tour was awesome. Our guide was like a walking Almanac, he could give google competitive with how knowledgeable he was. I learned so much on this tour. Windsor was just gorgeous. Stonehenge was epic and Bath was quaint. The Lacock Inn was historic but I wasn't overly impressed with the food quality. The bus was clean and comfortable and our driver was very nice. He gave a warm greeting to every guest. I am so glad and I took this tour and would do so again.

Outstanding, relaxing way to visit these iconic places. You don't get to spend a very long time at each but it's enough to get a really good overview, take lots of pictures and make memories. Highly recommend it!

This is a very organized tour our Tour Guide Eugene was exemplary very witty and knowledgeable. It was worth every minute.
Windsor Caste, Bath and Stonehenge. He was honest enough to to let us know that this trip is a good intro to London, which really is what I was expecting. The Driver Rushelle was a safe driver as well and sweet. Over all it is a great experience taking the tour with Premium tours, I am glad that I chose you guys.
Thank you.

We took this tour the last week of August. We toured Windsor Castle, went to the city of bath and explored the town, had a late lunch in Lacock and ended the day at Stonehenge. The tour guide was really good, he was very knowledgeable and also enjoyable to listen to. He provided context on historic and current events, and I really learned a lot about England from him. We did not tour the Roman bath’s in Bath, but instead went into the Bath ABbey, which I would highly recommend. I would definitely recommend this tour.. (#79), its a full day but not overwhelming.

Great trip, just wish there was more time to spend at each location. From London it was 12 hours round trip, most of it on the bus. Still had a great time and learned a lot. I would recommend it as a must for any first time travler.

Each stop on the twevelve hour tour offered a unique perpsective of the Engilsh country side and history. Stonehenge shows some ancient history and religious beliefs. Windsor shows one of the residences of the current monarchy. The town of Lacock shows what a 13th century town looks like and where many movies were filmed. Bath shows some famious salt baths from roman times. The bus driver and tour guide were amazing.

I loved this tour, Pepe(I think that's his name) our guide was so engaging, full of information and funny too, Andreas our driver was excellent also.
The one thing I would change is maybe the meeting point at Victoria coach station, a bit chaotic I think, anyway, there are no toilets inside bus so be sure to use it at station before you go in the bus as it will take about 1&1/2 to 2 hours before you arrive at Windsor castle, right there you will see toilets right by the entrance on the right, the castle is just beautiful, you can buy souvenir there and theres also an ice cream shoppe in the castle"s grounds..Right outside there's shopping and food if you have time before you board the bus again and head to Stonehenge, which is about another hour drive, toilets and food as well there
I would suggest taking water or buying some as you will be doing some walking at all locations, my favorite part of the tour was Bath, it is just an enchanted town, so beautiful, there are pubs, lots of restaurants and shopping there, then finally Lacock, pub food was good, the town itself is tiny but super interesting. Overall great tour!

We took a tour to Windsor, Bath, and Stonehenge with lunch in Lacock. It was a long day, but worth it if you have limited time. Unfortunately, Windsor was so crowded that day that we did not even have a chance to do the audio tour. You cannot control the crowds, so we saw as much as we could. Bath was absolutely beautiful and I wished that we had a chance to spend a lot more time there. Lunch was much better and enjoyable than a boxed lunch! Stonehenge was amazing to see when you consider when it was created. We had enough time at that location. It was a great highlight tour! Now that I have done it, I would recommend going to Windsor on your own via the train. It’s a beautiful little town to explore along with the castle. Lots of shops and eateries. I would recommend spending at least a half day in Bath and a couple of hours at Stonehenge. Bath also has amazing shops and eateries along with the Roman Bath House and an amazing cathedral to explore. It’s approximately a two hour ride from London.

Great trip! I had been to Stonehenge, Bath and Windsor before but my mom and daughter had not. We loved everything we saw, just wished the day were longer so we could have spent more time in each spot. Eugene was really upbeat, funny and knowledgeable. I really fell in love with Lacock and the historic pub where we had lunch. We all chose a different option and everyone's meals were great.

My only criticism/advice to future tour attendees: It's very confusing to find the correct station and bus. We came within about 60 seconds of being left because there are two bus stations very close to each other. Also, there was no guidance or instruction on what to do when get to the correct place. If we had not run out into the garage where the buses were waiting and grab a stranger to ask for help, we would have been left behind. I totally understand the need to leave on schedule. I just would have appreciated some additional guidance about meeting the correct bus and tour.

We have always been skeptical when it comes to bus tours. And we have never taken one, until this one! Oh, what a pleasant surprise. From the beginning until the end everything was great!
Our tour guide Derek and our driver Daniel were fantastic. Derek is one of the most knowledgeable people I have ever met. He is full of funny stories and knows so much about the area, the royal family and everything UK related you might want to know about.
We visited the Windsor Castle, where Derek waited in line with us until the castle opened up and walked us up to the entrance. Then we had some free time to wonder around the castle and the surrounding area. Then we were off to Stonehenge. Again, we had plenty of time to explore, take all the pictures that we wanted and such. Off to lunch in Lacock afterwards. On our way there Derek took everyone's order, so lunch was ready and waiting for us when we arrived. It was delicious! We were very happy with our choices of fish and chips and vegetarian mushroom risotto. Lacock is such a quaint little village. Derek gave us a little walk through the main streets and again he had many stories and gave us great information about the place. Last stop for the day was Bath. What an amazing town. I am so glad that we took this tour. Everything was just perfect. Job well done, guys! I feel like we really got our money's worth!
Thanks for a great experience!

This is a great day trip out of the city and see the countryside.

Our meeting time at the Victoria Coach stations was at 7:45 am, we made it at 7:41am! This was because we weren't familiar with the area and that the underground station is in a different building. We left on time.

Our guide Lucy & driver Tony were brilliant. They were able to keep the schedule on time within 5 minutes.

Windsor Castle: My husband & I opted out of touring Windsor Castle, however our bus was the first in the tour bus parking lot, a good sign. Those in our group who chose to take the tour enjoyed being first in line; Great way to get those photos in without other people in them. My husband & I chose to have a traditional English breakfast nearby (not included with tour) & explored the immediate area. We enjoyed the stroll around town.

Stonehenge: Again, our bus was the only one on the parking lot. That meant there weren't many people at the actual site, we got an hour to take in the sights and photos.

Lacock: Lunch at the St. George Inn, you had a choice of fish & chips, sausage & chips, or a meat pie that I forgot the exact name. Drinks were excluded, and came out of your own pocket unless it was still water. We also had a little bit of free time to explore. This town has been used as a filming location for the Harry Potter movies, the house by the church with the private sign was used as Potter's parents home & another house down the main road with a green door as the house Prof. Slughorn was hiding in the movie "HP & the half-blood prince"

Bath: Do go to the Roman baths, it's an cool place to see and a lot of interesting info on its history. You do get to try the water towards the end of the tour, but it's an acquired taste, that I didn't acquire.

I decided to break away from my group and do some sight seeing on my own. This was an excellent all day trip and I got to see a ton of London and the surrounding area. Make sure to pack snacks and water, since lunch is served late around 3pm. Also, don't get stuck at Stonehenge! you have to be in the shuttle line at least 30 minutes before you have to be back on the bus. If not, you risk being left behind! That happened to a couple of people on my tour. That leaves you about 15-20 minutes to take pictures, but that should be enough.

Bath was the low light of my tour, not much to see for me, but others seemed to enjoy it.

We did the tour last week. Steve was our tour guide. He was very entertaining and knowledgeable.
We were one of the first groups to get to Windsor Castle. We had plenty of time to do the entire tour of the castle, church and grounds. We were given audio sets for our tour when we got there.
It a very very long walk from the bus to the castle. Very fast paced to get there before the lines. We had several older and handicapped people who had a very hard time keeping up.
We were told at the beginning of our bus ride that this was a time limited tour and if any of us ran late at one stop it was going to make us late for the next. Stonehenge was our last stop so we were reminded we would be getting there at sunset right at their closing time so it was important for everyone to be back at the bus at the times given. All of our group were very punctual and no one ran late at any stop. It is a double decker bus with about 60 or so people.
Bath was our second stop. It’s a cute town. We toured Bath Abbey which is gorgeous! We tried to do the tour of the Roman Baths. This is not included in the price of the tour. It was very crowded and hot. No way to see any of it really. There is only one way in and one way out so trying to get around people to get out was difficult. I wish we had spent our time exploring the town instead.
Our next stop was Lacock. It’s a cute little town that some of Harry Potter and Downtown Abbey is filmed at. Charming old houses. We had lunch at a cute little pub that has been there forever. We chose our food choices before we got off the bus so it could be ready when we got there. Choice of fish and chips, shepherd’s pie and a vegetarian dish. This is all covered in the price of the tour. Beer is extra.
Had time to take some photos of the village before we left.
Last stop was Stonehenge. You get an audio tour here. Make sure you leave it at the visitor center before you go back to the bus. When you get off the bus there you are given a ticket for the shuttle. Which is a very nice bus! It picks you up right where the bus lets you out. It’s a short walk from the shuttle to the stones. Even though we weren’t allowed to be right up at the stones the area behind the rope is plenty close. I’ve done the tour that lets you in the circle and this was just as good. Being there at sunset was a very special thing. The sky was beautiful! The rolling hills all around are just gorgeous.
We had lots of time for the gift shop and tour of the exhibits.
The ride back to the city is plenty of time to work on all the great photos you have taken or to get a nap in.
Steve made sure to come around to each person on the bus to see where they wanted off at. There are two choices. Each are new tube entrances. We chose the one near the theater area since there were so many nice restaurants to grab dinner at before heading back to our rooms. Steve recommended some nice ones to choose from.
This is a long day. But it’s advertised as such so it should not be a surprise to anyone. Its well worth it.
I thought it gave us enough time to see all the things we wanted except the Roman Baths. I think we would have had time for those if we had skipped the Abbey. But the Abbey was beautiful! Again the little city of Bath is gorgeous. Wish we had just explored it instead of the Baths.
It is a double decker bus. Nice seats. They do not lean back though. I advise taking some drinks and snacks with you for the day. Lunch wasn’t till around 3:00 and you don’t really have time to grab anything at the stops.
This tour was a great way of seeing the most iconic places in 1 day. There is enough time scheduled for each location. Highly recommended.

We took this tour and although it was a heavy day, it was well worth it! I'm sorry to say that I cannot recall if our tour guide's name was either Scott M or Steve M, but he was amazing! He had so much information to give on each location (and in between) that even though I was sleepy on the bus, I forced myself to stay awake so that I don't miss anything that he said. I even found myself writing things down. He was just so knowledgeable.

We had 3 small children with us, and although they were dead tired by the end of the day, they did well. There just was so much to learn!

I rated the tour a 4/5 based on the sites visited rather than the overall experience which left something to be desired.
We experienced 4 stops including Windsor castle, StoneHenge, Bath and a visit to a pub for lunch. While again the sites were great, the problem is the amount of time you have at each stop is insufficient and very rushed. To give you an example, we arrived at Windsor Castle and got through a long security line at 10:10 am. The tour guide said we had to be out of there by 10:50 giving us 40 minutes total to see the castle. We ran to the doll house and after the line and seeing the attraction, we had 10 minutes left and had to run back to the bus.
I would recommend the tour add another hour and it would be perfect

Although Windsor Castle was closed for Prince Harry’s wedding preparations, Hampton Court Palace was a more than acceptable substitute. The day was beautiful (very un-English weather) and so were the locations. Best of all were our tour guide, Leon, and his driver sidekick, Martin. Martin is a tremendously skilled driver who saved us wait times more than once with his superior knowledge of alternate routes and drop-off/pick-up spots. He also has a wicked wit, based on the few utterances Leon cared to share with us.

Leon deserves his own mention as undoubtedly the best tour guide we’ve ever had. His knowledge of the sites we saw was complete, but better still were the tidbits of local knowledge he shared that enriched the whole day’s experience. He is thoughtful and kind and seemed to care deeply that each passenger had a most pleasant and memorable day. Almost unbelievably, he accomplished all this while displaying a keen wit that had us in stitches a good bit of the day.

On the whole, this trip was a bargain for our entertainment pounds and we would do it all again, if we could select Leon and Martin for our hosts. The only disappointing thing was the lunch in Lacock. The village was interesting, but the food at the pub was not up to the standards of the rest of the outing.

Can't say enough good about this one-day whirlwind of travel, beauty, and information. Our tour guide, Lucy, was aMAZing, and driver Richard was efficient and safe. My husband and I are both teachers and are usually the ones organizing and herding the masses, so it was a real treat for someone else to be in charge, hand us tickets, tell us where to go and when, etc. Lucy gives details ranging from archaelogical theories of Stonehenge to what foods not to take on the bus to keep fellow passengers happy. :-) She said from the outset that we'd only get a "taste" of each location, but we felt that she was able to give us more than that. Of course all three destinations each deserve their own day, but since we were in from the States and only had a few days total, we decided to give this a try and were not disappointed. If you are willing and able to power-walk, you'll see more at each location (e.g. our family walked very briskly through Windsor castle and were able to see the chapel, hall, and dollhouse). Could never have traveled to all three places in one day as efficiently or inexpensively on our own--good value as well as lovely sites.

As a solo traveler I found this to be a great way to take in a lot of sites in a short timeframe. This is a packed tour. Be sure to listen to the guides advice as I found myself with much more to see at Windsor Castle and rushing to get back to the bus. The guide was very knowledgeable about all the sites and shared some great insight. I appreciated the short rest periods in between sites as I had some jet lag. The Premier bus did not have the ability to charge your cell phone so unless you have really long battery life plan to bring some kind of backup. Lacock was very charming and the pub had a nice atmosphere. Overall, I really enjoyed this tour and would definitely go back to Windsor Caste for another look.

We met at Victoria Street Coach station (about 10 minutes walk from Victoria Station, be aware that the coach station is quite large and very busy and the boards did not clearly display this trip. The information line mid way through the station was lengthy and appeared not to move forward at all). Once we established we were in the right location and queue, Tara our guide was very informative. With decent flowing traffic through London, we were the 2nd tour bus to arrive at Windsor Castle however had to wait somewhat until the official opening time (no one can predict what London traffic will be like). Upon undertaking the normal security checks and measures, we were handed headsets and walked through public access of the palace starting with the dolls house. Beautiful! The Queen was in residence (not that we saw her of course) and we had plenty of time to see the public areas and spend time in gift shops as well as in the village. We could have gone into St Georges Chapel if we wished, I was surprised it was open to the public. Because of Tara's advice, we walked down to the village and were able to stand on the road corner to watch the changing of the Guard. All of our passengers arrived back at the coach on time and off we went to Bath for a short visit and self walk about. This does not include entrance to the Romans baths which I had hoped to see and we were warned to book while on the bus (via our mobiles using bus internet) to avoid the 1 hour long queues if we wanted to go. Over to Lacock for a very late (do eat morning tea at one of the little coffee shops in Bath) but delicious lunch served very promptly by staff. Onto Stonehenge, a bit of a personal let down and we thought a bit too much time was allowed here. Our coach driver allowed the early birds back onto the coach in the mizzling weather and once everyone was boarded it was back to London Two drop off stops were made for passengers to depart the bus as it would not be returning to Victoria Coach station. Be aware this was getting late and shops such as Waitrose were closed if you hope to purchase fixings for a meal.

Windsor Castle - we started off really early, 7:45am but unfortunately 5 more tourist buses are ahead of us. The line was already a bit long when we got there and we had to wait for a approximately an hour to enter the castle. So, we literally just had to run around the castle just to make it to the time given to us. My family didn't even get to enter the St. George Chapel. I just snap a photo and left for fear of being left behind.
Bath- time allotted was enough although i wished we did more of a walking tour too. Otherwise, we enjoyed the personal time.
Stonehenge - time enough for some selfies, restroom and shopping.
Lacock - supper is OK, the scenery is very nice. i wish there was more of walking tour or at least we were gathered to a spot listen to history of a building.

Overall all it was very enjoyable. Our guide took advantage of the bus ride to brief us with history. She was also very accommodating and understanding of our needs. Will most definitely recommend. I wonder how it could be if the sequence of the trip was different.

This tour was one of the most memorable things I did while in England. It was everything I expected from the description and more! Our tour guide was fantastic and we ended up being the first tour in line at Windsor Castle (which has huge lines). The only critiques I have are that I wish there was more time at each place because there is so much to do (however this isn’t possible for a day trip) and the food at the old pub in Lacock was just alright, nothing fantastic, but the historic town makes up for it 100%. 5 star tour!

This tour is jam packed. Our tour guide Alan was AMAZING! He really made the tour. I enjoyed all the sights and food. Definitely recommend this tour. Its worth it. I will say if you really want to see the Roman baths this may not be the tour for you. We got there within the last 10 minutes and had to rush through it.

I really liked the tour, although sometimes it felt that we could have spent more time on one site.
The issue is that there are no toilets on the bus.
Our guide, however, was really excellent. Passionate, full of humour and friendly.

Our expectations of this trip were absolutely exceeded. Dan and Malcom were fantastic. Dans commentary and guidance was excellent and had just the perfect amount of sass, information and entertainment. We would definitely recommend. The best way to do all these places in one day!

This was an amazing tour. Yes, it was a long day but we got to see and learn so much in the time we had that the experience was well worth it!! Our tour guide Dan was very informative and knowledgeable and also had a great sense of humor in telling the history and stories at all the places we visited. I loved all the places we toured and even had some nice surprises along the way. The drive itself through the beautiful english country side was just breathtaking. Stonehenge was something we were very much looking forward too. It did not disappoint, it was simply inspiring. We arrived there as the sun was low in the sky which set the scene for beautiful pictures. Dinner was a happy surprise in Lacock. Food orders were taken on the bus and ready for us when we arrived. I'm glad we got to experience that lovely pub and town. The Roman Baths in Bath was a beautiful surprise. We paid the extra fee to go inside and explore the ruins. I highly recommend this visit!!
Loved the full day, it is well WORTH it !!!

Premium Tours nailed this tour. Our guide graduated in Archaeology. She was a wealth on information. Windsor castle was a favorite part of our trip. Did wish we had more time in Bathe. Lacock was used to film some of Harry Potter. The meal in this town was great.
highly recommended, it was a fantastic day in Stonehenge windsor castle, you must absolutely visit it. (i recommend to take a tour guide)

Viator handled our reservation and they make it very confusing so that you don’t really understand what you have paid for. It said “ Stonehenge” was included but when we got to Stonehenge we had to wait in line for quite a while and buy tickets! Very disappointed and will not use viator in the future!!

We, 3 adults, had a FANTASTIC Day with our Tour Guide ANN MARIE, visiting Windsor, Stonehenge, Bath & a Pub Lunch in the historic town of Lacock. Prepare yourself for a long day as it is an aggressive itinerary. But to visit these historic places in 12 hours, it is well worth the effort and the very reasonable price considering your admission to Windsor Castle, Stonehenge, and a genuine delicious hot lunch at a historic old Pub in Lacock is included.... note:Bath is on your own, although it is a lovely town to explore & enjoy on your own should you choose to skip the Bath in Bath.😊. In my personal experience when traveling on such an all day Coach Tour, accept upfront that you are only going to get a “taste” of the experiences & environs, it really comes down to the knowledge and personality of your Tour Guide (and driver). It can very well be a hit or a miss, that then decides if your 12 hour day is a Long 12 hours, or, where-did-the-time-go 12 hours. With Ann Marie as our Tour Guide, we definitely marked a HIT! Ann Marie is so friendly, knowledgeable, accommodating, &, just as important, runs a tight ship in keeping the day on schedule. Fortunately, Ann Marie kept the day well balanced in we were able to see what we came (and paid for) to see, yet left us wanting to come back and see more some day.

My recommendation in making this long day a bit more comfortable is to pack something accessible to eat/drink between sight seeing, as it is a long time until lunch... about 3:00. Considering that you board the Coach at 7:30am, you WILL get hungry & thirsty along the way. And while Stonehenge and Windsor Castle offer an opportunity for a quick bite & drink, there is no time to enjoy either at a leisurely pace. Pack something in your bag/backpack. You will be very glad you did
It was good. Long ride, lunch was good. Weather was Chilly but Leon and his driver were great! Definitely recommend!
My husband and I did this tour and it was great! Our tour guide, Omar was really nice and very knowledgeable on the different places we visited. Highly recommended!

The experience wad great! Everything was on time. Our guide was very nice and helpful. Is worth it! This is our first time here in London and i already love it! People are very nice and friendly. The countryside is beautiful. Those valleys are amazing. I highly recommend this tour.

My sister and I enjoyed this tour very much. Anna Maria was our tour guide and she was very informative and very interesting to listen to. Andre did a fabulous job driving the coach especially maneuvering around the traffic on the highway. Windsor Castle was amazing to see. I would have liked to spend more time at Windsor but we were on a tight schedule. Stonehenge and Bath were also interesting to see.

My wife and I went on this tour this week while in London and were very happy with it. The tour guide was great and the bus driver excellent. We toured Windsor Castle (amazing), Stonehenge (interesting history, though not very exciting) and Bath. Pub lunch was served in the oldest pub in the UK (1300's). This is a long day, just be prepared for this! All worth it though!

My husband and I took this trip on 11/24, and we are so glad that we did! We got to see so much in just one day. Our tour guide Peter was funny, energetic and had vast knowledge of each stop's history. You can certainly tell that history is his passion, and he brings it with him on each tour. I felt like I had learned so much about England on this trip. I loved every minute of it.
Its a long day, and there is not a minute to spare, him and Abdul kept us right on schedule with no issues at all.

(NOTE - drivers in London are tracked by hours, so being on time is a MUST. If you are not on time and the driver goes over their allotted hours, you will have to pull over and wait for a new driver to come relieve you. If you are hours away from London, this will be very inconvenient for everyone on board. Please be courteous to people on your tour, your driver and your guide and be on time for each departure.)

TIPS:
Most coaches do not allow hot food or drink. This was the one tour where this was an exception, however, plan your day in advance. If you need coffee/tea, finish it before the bus departs.
Eat breakfast!!!! This is a long day, you will stop for lunch, but that may be later in the afternoon.
Pack a snack and drinks - you are allowed to bring sandwiches and cold beverages on coaches, plan ahead. (I Stopped at Eat. and Pret on each of my tours and grabbed a sandwich, chips and a bottle of water and had no issues all day with hunger/thirst)
When we stopped in Windsor, we were able to grab some food. If you can not get it before your tour departs London, get something in Windsor to hold you over until you get to Lacock.

My title says it all! We were hurried from the time we left until we got to Stonehenge. I wanted to see the church, where Harry & Megan were married, so we didn't get to see Windsor Castle. The village was so cute but we didn't get to spend any time there either. I'm guessing we had about 1/2 hour in Bath. Not enough time to see the baths. We quickly ran through the church, across from the baths, and then it was time to get back on the bus. The only place we got to spend any time was at Stonehenge. I was grateful for that since that was my priority. We were the last bus of the day so we had beautiful light for pictures. Our tour guide was excellent (sorry, I can't remember her name) and our lunch was OK. A cute little pub with decent food. Trying to pack too much into a one-day tour. Skip Bath perhaps!

This was the perfect trip to take when you have limited time in London and want to experience the countryside, cute pubs, Stonehenge and Windsor Castle. Our guide and driver were great! Very informative and patient with all guests. He was definitely entertaining as well.

Our tour guide was Eugene and the driver was Carlos. The first stop was Windsor Castle I’m glad we didn’t purchase a ticket to go in because there would have only been one hour to tour. We walked around the village and enjoyed all the shops. We also we’re lucky enough to see the changing of the guard. From there we went to Stonehenge. There are no words! It is absolutely amazing. The only complaint was that there wasn’t enough time to soak it all in, an extra half an hour would have been perfect. We stopped at a pub and Laycock for a great lunch then as we drove out of the area we saw a house that was used in one of the Harry Potter films and a field that was used for Braveheart. The last stop was Bath. We did not purchase a ticket to go inside the Roman bags but Eugene showed us the bath area through a window and gave us all the history!

The itinerary was very packed, but I think the time was well spent. Gavin was extremely knowledgeable, helpful, and enthusiastic, and Carlos provided a great ride. Staying in London is nice and all for experiencing a new place, but getting to see Windsor Castle, Bath, and Stonehenge really makes for a good reminder that this place is the place of history textbooks.

This is a great trip. Transportation was comfortable. Sites were amazing. Tour guide Eugene was very knowledgeable and driver Andre gave us a comfortable ride. A little more time would be good at each location but understand it is a lot to cover in one day.

What an awesome group! Lucy our tour guide was top notch and our driver was fast fantastic. Felt safe the whole time we were on this trip. Learned new items about the area even though I had taken this same tour 8 years ago. Loved it and would do it again

A Visit to London isn't "really complete" until one has had the opportunity to visit the smaller/historical towns, the lovely countryside, and an example of the UK's "ancient history. However, arranging this can be quite complicated-- but this 1 (very full) day tour is ideal! Windsor is a "town" located near Windsor Castle, while Bath was a Roman Town... and Stobehenge is from the "Pre-History period"! The opportunity to eat at an historic country pub is like "icing on a cake". The drivers are very skilled and the tour guide provides much really interesting background information. I would highly recommend this tour as it is a very efficient way to experience a broad array of what a visit to the attractions near London and environs have to offer.

I hope that this Review has been interesting!

Took a day tour from London. Stonehenge was included. Definitely worth it! Not to many people in October so that was nice. Nice cafe inside. Shuttle was provided but can walk too. My husband and I really enjoyed this trip to Stonehenge.
Would have loved to have more time at Windsor Castle and Bath. Lacock and lunch was a very nice addition. Stonehenge is a you see it and leave kinda thing for me.

With the onslaught of protesters taking over the city streets, we did not feel it was safe to meet the tour bus at the designated place. The tour office did not respond to our inquiry.
We were told, days later, that they thought it was safe so no refund would be given.

Fabulous day with Leon as our guide and Carlos as our driver. It didn't feel like long to get to each destination with Leon around. He was absolutely both hilarious and informative. Very engaging!
Yes it is a long tour / day but an awesome way to see some great sites in London. We thoroughly enjoyed each destination and Leon gave us great info and suggestions on the best way to use our time at each location. Thank you so much again to Leon and Carlos.

The sites were interesting, but it made for a very long day. I attempted to find an expected end time for the tour but wasn't able to find the information on the site. It turned out to be 13 hours from pick up to drop off. If you aren't interested in paying to see the Roman baths, there is a lot of time to kill in Bath.

Ours was a tad different. We went to Oxford instead of Bath. Great tour and guide. I will say that if you have anyone who cannot keep up with the group and needs to move at a slower pace, either let your guide know or find another leisurely tour. There's plenty of time on these tours but it's better to be safe and ask. We didn't get to go into Windsor due to losing our group. My Mom cannot walk at a fast pace so we missed out on it but it was also our fault for not communicating this to our guide.
Fantastic day. John a wonderful guide. Toilets at Stonehenge the most disgraceful I’ve seen in all my travels. Inexcusable

Our tour guide Peter and driver Carlos were marvelous in providing a great experience for us on this trip. Peter provided interesting historical information regularly on the tour and worked very hard to make us all comfortable. He also kept us on time... difficult with big groups, but necessary. I would travel with again any time!
Highly recommended. Awesome snapshot of the area and guide was sensational. Great way to spend the day. Loved it and would recommend it to everyone as a must do. New coach

Yes it is a full day but we wanted to see all these sites and didn’t have multiple spare days to visit. Tom our guide was fantastic! He was informative and funny. Our driver was very good too. At Windsor we chose not to enter the castle but to explore the town instead which we enjoyed. We even walked to Eton College and back with plenty of time. At Stonehenge we got soaked with rain but were still in good spirits because of Tom. Bath was short but we still saw the highlights. The pub lunch in Laycock was changed to pub dinner on our way back to London and we actually proffered this. The village is lovely and the food was good. Thanks Tom for a great day!

The places they took you by coach bus is fascinating, however, they didn't have wifi on their bus as they write in the tour inclusion. Also, they cover three places on this trip but gives very less time to roam around or explore always gets less than 2 or 2 hours to explore the place. Be cautious they really leave if you are late by 5 min. One family with two kids they were late at Windsor castle and they left them but the good thing is that family joined us later on in the same bus.

For Roman Bath ticket is not included so you have to buy which is quite expensive about GBP 54.50 for 2 adults a kid. that was an extra expense for this tour

About the guided tour is a myth in this trip that Lady I guess her name was Lucy gives you commentary in the bus, will take you every place and show you around just gives you heads up and then you are on your own. But you see other companies are giving a guided tour with headphones etc. for the large group (like us we were 84 in that coach bus) for the same type of coach buses.

For the lunch was good but the portion was very small even with the fish and chips the fish was smaller and the chips were like 10-15 pieces, and fish & chips supposed to be the stapled food for the country.

Throughly enjoyed this tour. Our tour Guide, Aaron, did his best to inform, entertain and engage his tour group. Enjoyed everyplace we visited though Bath was less organized. Not enough time for the Roman bath tour so just wandered the quaint town for an hour. Would have enjoyed more time at Windsor Castle and Stonehenge but not sure how that could have happened without cutting Bath or lunch. Lunch was good but didn’t get it until 3:30. We were very hungry by then as we had to leave to catch the tour before 8am. LONG day but worth it.

This trip needs to be re-thought and re-designed. It should be noted in the description that there is VERY LITTLE time at each destination. For what we paid, I was a bit disappointed in this experience. Just about every part of the trip was a mad rush. The departure from Victoria Station was pure chaos. It was very crowded, hot, and disorganized; very hard to tell if you're in the right place. Bathroom was not in operation on the bus, as was advertised. This may have solved some of the rushing around and precious time we wasted finding restrooms at the tourist destinations.

Trip to Windsor was far too brief. We had to practically run to keep up with our tour guide, Gavin, which was not easy, as my mom has bad knees. A lot of walking on this tour, which I think needs to be mentioned more prominently. We then waited over a half hour to get into Windsor Castle, in the sun. Very little time to see the State Apartments, which were a bit underwhelming. Had 5 minutes to see the chapel where Meghan and Harry were married. Did not have time to see the changing of the guard or to browse the many shops there. We had time to purchase sandwiches for the bus ride, as we were told lunch would now be dinner.

On to Stonehenge. Had about 15 minutes to quickly walk around the stones, and hopped back on the tram to the visitors' center. No time to visit the visitor center and giftshop, which was very disappointing. Had time to use the bathroom and run yet again back to the bus, which we had trouble locating. When I mentioned our disappointment to Gavin, his response was well, there are other tours. While the design of the day was not his fault, it was a flippant and dismissive answer. Others on the bus we spoke with didn't even have time to use the bathroom, and didn't get to see the visitors' center, either. Hugely disappointing.

Bath was lovely. Very picturesque, and we were able to browse through the shops. Again, this was not very long, but better compared to other stops.

Finally on to Lacock. The meal was just ok. We left hungry, as it was not a very large portion. Too much time at this location; Gavin took the group on a walking tour of the village, which we skipped, as there wasn't much to see at all. Boring. The time wasted in Lacock would have been better spent and Windsor and Stonehenge.

Was pleased with the drop off location near Cromwell Rd, near our hotel.

Gavin was a great guide. Funny and informative, and it's not his fault the tour was designed in this way. I would have felt more comfortable if he has stayed with our tour group, as there were times we felt lost and weren't sure where to go. We were basically on our own at each location.

For the money, we were disappointed. Trip description needs updating to better reflect what the trip entails.

This tour was an excellent way to get acquainted with some of the important sites in England’s countryside. Because you’re visiting so many places, you only spend about one hour at each place. Stonehenge only takes an hour, but all of the other sites can easily be a day trip. Our guide, Robin, was very knowledgeable and entertaining. He got us to each site quickly and helped us get the best views possible. I strongly recommend this tour.

A great Day Long Tour that included plenty of personal walk about about time well balanced with the informational Guided tour provided by Eugene our Guide.Eugene was an excellent and knowledgeable guide. You cant pack more History into a tour in 1 day. Highly recommended.
Our tour guide Andrew and driver Matt were amazing. Andrew is very enthusiastic and entertaining. My family and I loved this tour.

This fast paced tour was great for my son and I. Not a lot of time at anyone spot which we liked as we like to see things and move on. Not a tour for people who really like to dive deep but for us it was great!

We just finish the tour to Windsor, Bath, Stonehenge, and Laycock. The guide Eugene and driver Tur Guy were perfect. They made everything run smooth. The sites were perfect and easy. The tour leaves early but it is worth it. You get to Windsor before it opens making the viewing easy. The only negative comment is the dishes other then Fish and Chips for lunch are a little meager. Also, it is a long day, bring snacks or buy food along the way.

Our tour guide, Eugene was absolutely outstanding for this trip -- very informative, pointed out sights as we drove, gave a lot of history, kept us on time, was very pleasant the whole time. Our drive, Abdul was amazing getting us down very narrow roads and did so comfortably! The bus did have a restroom on board which was nice, but there was time to go at the stops. We arrived at Windsor castle before sit opened so we were one of the first groups in, there was enough time to see everything plus do some shopping at the shops nearby. Bath was very nice, lovely shops and pubs, wish we had more time but completely understand this is a tour and can't spend the day. Our lunch at the pub in Lacock was excellent and we had time to walk around. Stone henge was nice also and plenty of time to see it. We were dropped off at either of two bus stations which was very nice!. Definitely recommend this tour.

First, Magnus our guide was fantastic. It is important to know you will get very very small exposure to each area. At Windsor we waited in The queue for 1 hour just to get in. We have 1 hour to get back to the bus. In Bath, Magnus walked us to the Abby, which was beautiful but don’t expect to see the Roman baths, there is no time. Lacock you will have time for lunch and a few minutes to explore. Final, Stonehenge, you will have about 1.5 hours which seemed to be enough. Windsor and bath I would recommend doing on there own.

Hi, if you're looking at this review then you're probably still deciding if it's worth the money etc etc. Short answer is yes, long answer follows.

The tour of these three iconic locations was part of a whirlwind 1 week visit to England as part of my wife's bucket list holiday.

The tour starts at the Victoria Coach Station which is about a 10 minute unhurried walk from Victoria Street underground and then in the evening we were dropped at a passenger voted underground, I think it was Gloucester Road?

Coach was brand new with driver 'Torgay' and guide 'Leon'. Actual drive was uneventful and smooth provided by an obviously skilled driver.

Now Leon...I am being kind and truthful by best describing our day as being a fun filled day with Leon which happened to include visits to the three sites. Leon is a quick witted, funny, likeable rogue who has an encyclopedic amount of facts and trivia of London, the sites and the Royal Family and destined to have his own tv show. Transit between the sites was as expected laborious but Leon's continual informative/fun patter made the time pass quickly.

As other reviewers have said, actual time at the sites can be a bit of a rush but it is what it is. Windsor castle and Bath are the highlights and I'm inclined to suggest giving stonehenge a miss if the budget is tight.

The meal at the pub in Laycock was very average but in general I found nearly all food around London as very expensive, very average and not much on the plate. I had the cod and chips and the cod had an encrustation of batter that could have been used on the space shuttle for shield repairs.. Also, had a pie and peas/mash at a 'pie shop' near the Royal Maritime Museum (chose the beef pie on recommendation of a customer) and to my dismay, found the filling to be just gravy and that superfine mince (down to 5 microns etc) that could have been anything. If you want a decent pie, come to Australia.

I guess the other guides are great as well but if you score Leon, it's going to be a good day.

best wishes John

I have enjoyed the day and I find it very practical if you don’t have enough time . It covers wide range . It isn’t very relaxing, it involves fast walking if you would like to cover as much as possible. I wish we could stretch a day and could spend more time at each stop.
We started our day at Windsor and we managed to cover most of it , but we walked very fast. That was my favourite part. Than we headed to Bath and again I wish we would have more time there as well , I enjoyed it a lot . Very last bit was Stonehenge and it was outstanding.
Our tour guide was Frank and driver Andrej, they did a really good job .
My next tour will book with Premium tours .

This tour is worth every penny you spend, the bus was really nice and clean, our tour guide was Ben (Big Ben) and our driver was Tony, they were both very courteous and friendly, we visited all four locations with plenty of time to take pictures, I personally had time to sit at a nice cafe at Windsor and at bath and enjoy some coffee and treats while I waited to depart to the next destinations. Very well organized trip, lunch was scheduled as we rode to the pub and it was ready when we arrived, food was delicious! Must do this trip if you’re in London for a few days and are looking to visit multiple l historical locations outside of London within one day.

We had a wonderful day on this tour! Our tour guide Eugene was absolutely fantastic and he was very knowledgeable about all three locations. The day ran very smoothly and our driver James was great. Would have been nice to have longer at each place but totally understandable as to why we couldn't. (don't be the person that's late back at each stop it puts the whole group out) Overall a brilliant day and would HIGHLY recommend

I only had one day, so chose this tour. Parts were exceptional, other parts could use improvement.
Our guide Tom was fun, thoughtful and knowledgeable.
Our driver was a pro with the double-decker bus. Good thing, because there were narrow spaces and long stretches of driving.
I saw Hampton Court. (Windsor was closed)
PRO: It was well presented for it’s great expanse. King Henry VIII lived there quite a bit.
CON: We only had 1 hr. Which was “enough” if you skim thru, but not enough time to do the Audio Tour,
Stonehenge was jaw dropping. The observation walk is set so that 90% of the best views and angles, can be photographed with no people seen in them.
Locke was our lunch stop., with a limited menu. The lager was good! My lunch was so-so. We had a walk around the ancient town, then took off for Bath,

Arriving Bath after 5 PM was a big bummer, The Roman baths and shops were closed, and it was hard to find a toilet. It was touristy and not a lot of fun. I’m sure if we had arrived earlier, it wouldn’t have seemed like a waste of time. I recommend the tour skip Bath, and get back toLondon at a reasonable hour. I didn’t get back to my room until after 10PM.
I also think more English history could have been talked about over the long boring stretches of driving. The bus had no wifi, So I couldn’t look up anything about what I had learned and seen

This was a really nice tour for the price. Andrew was the tour guide and he was really great, kept things light and fun, provided lots of interesting information, and kept the group on time and on track. My only complaint is you do feel rather rushed when you get to each destination, but you’re fitting in a lot of stops within each day. If I had to do it again, I’d skip the lunch at Lacock in order to spend more time in Bath.

Gavin was an amazing tour guide that kept us well entertained And well informed. I learned so much. Got some breath taking photos and made some amazing memories. Everything was well organized and we got a little taste and so many places around England.

Our tour guide, Peter, and bus driver, Nuno were excellent hosts and provided very informative history for each site we visited.

We went to Hampton Court Palace instead of Windsor Castle due to the holiday but it was still a great tour.

The only thing I would say is that I felt we didn’t have a lot of time to explore Hampton Court Palace or Roman Baths. Might not make sense to have 3 places to cram into one day especially the distance to drive there and back.

We did the day tour that took us to Windsor Castle, Stonehenge and Bath. The tour was nice but the time allotted at each stop was not the best. First stop was Windsor Castle and we spent half the time waiting for the castle to open and then felt rushed going on the tour. Then Bath we barely had any time to do anything! Finally at Stonehenge we had way too much time. I would have liked less time at Stonehenge and more time at Bath. Also the pub lunch was good, but seemed very overpriced for what we got. Plus we ate lunch so late that everyone was starving. I would recommend not doing the included pub lunch.

As for the bus, it was VERY confusing where to go. The instructions only said Victoria Coach Station and we had no idea where to go once we got there. The tour also said there was free WiFi on the bus which is one of the reasons we chose this tour because we didn’t have phone plans and the WiFi was not working at all. When I asked the tour guide and bus driver about the WiFi, their answer was “sometimes it works sometimes it doesn’t”. I also reached out to Premium Tours about the WiFi and got the same answer. This is something they advertised and a reason we chose this company and were very disappointed.

I am glad we got to see so much in just one day but everything was very rushed to be able to see all the things listed on this tour. We really only got one hour in each location. We almost missed the Roman baths because we got to bath at 4:50 and the last entrance is at 5pm. If you want more time in these places I recommend another tour that would allow for it.

We had an enchanting day with Eugene as tour guide. His enthusiasm was evident and he was full of energy, information, and genuine friendliness for all the tour participants! Our tour was Monday in late March and the weather was lovely too. We knew it was just a 'taster' of the sights, so be aware that you'll wish you had about 30 more minutes at every stop. But this was a great way to see a ton of history and beauty in one very full day! Windsor castle was great, and we enjoyed it very much. The chapel is wonderful also. I wish the Queen Mary's Dolls House was open. I will have to come again when it re-opens. I was delighted that the Queen happened to be in residence on the day we visited. Stonehenge was next and be aware that it's windy there and you will want to dress warmly. The site is a distance from the museum, and you will want to ride the Stonehenge bus (the walkers we saw must not have been on a time limit). Going to Lacock was important to me, as I love period films featuring the streets of this historically preserved village. The lunch was after 3 pm. Lunch was good but not generous portions. It was nice to have a warm meal though! Last was Bath. We arrived around 4:45 pm, with an hour and 20 minutes to spend there. We were fascinated by the Roman Bath experience so chose to purchase tickets. I would highly recommend it if history/archeology are of interest to you. This tour was an outstanding experience (no late coming tour members, positive and engaging guide, and all was smooth and happy). We would definitely recommend this tour!

My wife and I choose to take this tour, our first ever organized tour while traveling, and what a great decision that was. We had the pleasure of enjoying the Frank and Lamar “team” on our tour, Frank was the guide and Lamar, the driver. For me personally, safety is a big issue and my wife and I agreed Lamar handled the driving duties very admirably. He was smooth in driving the bus and there was never a time we felt unsafe whatsoever . And the there was Frank! We really lucked out when they assigned Frank as our guide. He shared his vast amount of knowledge regarding English history in general and specifically about the four sites we visited, Windsor Castle, Stonehenge, the quaint 18th century village of Lacock where we enjoyed lunch and the city of Bath. Not only was Frank knowledgeable, but he is very friendly and has a great sense of humor. He really made a long and interesting day a really fun and memorable experience. Like other reviewers have shared, this tour is more of an overview of our stop locations, given how much is packed into one day.

Windsor Castle, the grand, beautiful and historic home to the Royal family and recent wedding location of Harry and Meghan. Tour of the State Apartments was self guided by castle policy, but employed an audio guide which was very informative.

The drive from Windsor castle to Stonehenge was equally informative and interesting. We passed the royal Ascot horse racing track where the yearly spectacle is held, learned tons of interesting facts, saw England’s equivalent of “Area 51”, and learned a story about the forgotten city of Imber, amongst others.

Stonehenge speaks for itself, incredible! While we were there the temperature was probably 30-40c with sustained winds of 40-50 miles an hour, brrrrr! Not much the Frank and Lamar team could do about that! With only 65 minutes to tour, we opted for coffee over the exhibits display before reboarding the bus.

Bath is a super cute and historic 18th century town. We didn’t visit the Roman Baths located there, which has a separate entrance fee, but instead strolled the streets enjoying the many cafes, pubs and shops. A short visit, but very glad we got to see it.

Finally a late lunch in Lacock. Honestly, lunch was good,but nothing special, I had the tasty cottage pie. It was nice to chat with our other tour mates and The George Inn where lunch served was historically cool. But the town of Lacock itself is really picturesque and has a fascinating history which includes its current location for the filing of many popular TV shows and movies including Harry Potter and Downtown Abbey.

The long two hour ride back to London after leaving Lacock was fine, especially since we were on a comfortable brand new luxury coach. Not much to see once the sun dipped; some people slept, I wrote this review and edited pictures. After a “go-go busy day”, nice to kick back and relax and get ready to enjoy more London nightlife.

If you are considering this day trip adventure, we give it two thumbs up!

The tour was great, the guide, Gavin was great as well. I found him very enthusiastic and informative. I chose the option without Windsor Castle entry and at first being one of the very few people that wasn't going inside, I felt a bit lost of what to do in the meanwhile and wished I had chosen the option for the castle entry. Really for the price difference, if you're stuck trying to choose the option with or without the castle entry, I say just choose the castle entry to kill the time as you're there for like 3 hours and many of the stores are not open until about 9 am or 10 am. With the time to kill at Windsor, I started it off with walking around to see the different stores they had and find something I could do to pass the time. I started with breakfast in this cozy restaurant between a souvenir shop and the museum, unfortunately I forgot the name, but they had many options for hot breakfast, pastries, and hot drinks, which I was thankful for in the cold morning. Gavin, our guide, was great in providing information along the way to the other locations. He did just the right amount of talking, it wasn't overbearing that you can't catch a quick nap from one place to the other. If you're a Harry Potter fan, you will love the tour when it get's to Lacock, as Gavin was great at pointing out different houses, like Harry's biological parent's house and a couple of more things from the films. Even though the tour does not include the Roman Baths entry, it is not expensive at all and even one hour is still enough time to visit the Baths. End it off by taking a sip of the water at the designated location. It wasn't an awful taste, it taste just like a natural spring water to me. Overall I would definitely recommend the tour. Choose the different additions based on your preference and how you would like spend your free time. I was in England for a very short time, the first day being me coming central London via bus from France, the next day, doing this tour, and the following going back to France. All in all if it wasn't for this tour I wouldn't have seen much of England as I didn't get any chance to do any sightseeing my first evening in central London. The only thing I wish would change is the amount of time we stayed in Stonehenge. For me that was the biggest highlight and reason why I chose the tour but we weren't there for long. I had to quickly get out of the tour bus, use the restroom and catch the other bus to the site itself, after walking around the whole circle and stopping to listen to a few audio guides, I caught the bus back the the visitor's center but I barely had time to go through the small museum and see the old houses or ask any questions. So I think somehow the tour needs to be changed to given Stonehenge enough time for you to take everything in. I felt a bit rushed.

My first intention was not to take this tour, but the tour I wanted sold out. Since I was there had the time and took the chance, which was the BEST decision I could have done.
Gavin our tour guide was superb, lots of facts very knowledgeable and provided with key information on each site. I loved the tour and definitely will do it again.

Gavin is the best!

While in London we booked this as our only bus tour and were very happy with this decision. Frank was our guide, Nuno our driver and they were both amazing. Frank was so knowledgeable and had a great sense of humor that kept the entire bus laughing throughout. Nuno was a great driver and very nice every time we got on and off the bus. It is a very long day but worth it. You get just enough time in each location to explore. The lunch (we had the cottage pies) was delicious and the walk around Lacock back to the bus was an added bonus. In Bath we opted to go into the Roman Baths (which isn’t included in the tour cost) but it was worth it. Even had extra time to grab a snack for the bus ride back to London. The ride back was about two hours so you can sneak in a little nap. Frank came around to everyone on the bus asking where we were trying to get to so he could suggest which of the two drop offs would be best for everyone. He even gave directions to each group as we got off the bus where to walk towards to get to the underground and was giving restaurant recommendations if you asked. Tour locations were great, bus was clean, comfy, Frank and Nuno were awesome and would 100% recommend!!

A very well planned & informative tour from start to finish. Our tour guide was excellent and had a great sense of humor. Unfortunately, we overslept our alarm so we missed getting on at the start of the tour, but we were able to take an Uber to Windsor castle and catch up with the group. I don't recommend missing the bus as it was a very expensive Uber and since we were late getting there we missed the group tour of the castle and getting any quality time in the town, but managed to tour the abbey where Meghan and Harry were married which was beautiful. Next stop was Stonehenge. The history lesson on the way was very interesting. Since there's not much to do there other than view the rock formation and a quick stop in the tourist store, I wish the time there was a bit shorter so we could have had a bit more time in Lacock and much more time in Bath. Lacock has a fascinating history given its connection to the Harry Potter movies, and Bath was beautiful all lit up at night. Just wish we had more day light there and time to tour the museum and shop. Certainly will make a trip back when we can spend more time there.

This is a coach tour and I knew the drill - big group, limited time at each spot, stick to the schedule or be left behind, and plenty of time on the bus travelling between the spots. I didn’t have a lot of time in London and wanted to maximise my stay so this seemed to provide the best value in terms of what I was looking for.

Our tour guide was Lucy and our driver was Carlos. They’re an excellent team, with Lucy being very knowledgeable and provided lots of interesting trivia (including where to get luxury perfumes for your four-legged friends) and Carlos getting us safely to the different locations.

First stop was Windsor castle - we were first in the tour group queue, spent about 45 minutes waiting for the gates to open and it even started to rain. Yet it was well worth the effort when we saw the queues behind us with hundreds of people for other tour groups. Being first in the queue allowed us to maximise our hour there: more time in the castle, less time waiting to get in. We were advised to grab some snacks as lunch will be much later in the day.

Second stop was Stonehenge - be prepared - plenty of tourists and you probably won’t get the picture you wanted as there are plenty of people all around the structures. We had about just over an hour here, enough to go around the stone henge and the museums twice.

Lunch was around 3pm at Lacock’s St George’s Inn, a pub built in the 1300s. Lunch options were fish and chips, cottage pie or veggie risotto and drinks were paid for separately. I found lunch unremarkable and didn’t see any value stopping at Lacock - we could’ve gone straight to Bath and spent more time there. We were back to the bus and drove along interesting countryside sights such as thatched roof homes, military sites, and interesting local pub signs.

Last stop was Bath and we had again, just over an hour here which was far too short for such a lovely town. It was the last evening of the Christmas markets and there were also the Roman baths. Given the limited time, you had to chose between seeing the city or going to the Baths. I could have easily spent half a day there.

After this was a two hour drive back to London, arriving at about just past 8pm.

I knew what I was getting into and at least got some happy snaps of different sites near London. Be wary that there is very limited time at each location and you need to abide by the schedule. I would recommend skipping the lunch at Lacock option where possible and spend more time at Bath instead.
In May, went on the half-day tour to Stonehenge. The self-guided walking tour with audio narrative was very interesting insight into the history of the people who lived there thousands of years ago.

This was a very nice “highlight” tour. i really enjoyed the day, and all the sites we visited. the day strated early and the bus took us to first to Windsor castle, followed by Stonheadge. with a mid afternoon lunch at a nice traditional pub in a cute little village, then we finished in bath. While it would have been nice to have more time in each places to wander around, there is enough time to visit the main attractions.

If you’ve never been to these sights, this is the tour for you. It’s a long day but the tour is quick, lots of walking, and introduces you to the sites. This tour prepares you just in case you want to go back on your own.

Tour started around 7:45am and we were not back into London until almost 10:00pm. Needless to say, it was a very long day. Due to the lines at Windsor Castle, we were only able to spend about an hour exploring the grounds. We stood in line for about 30 minutes to get through the security line, as there were several other tour groups there. I know this couldn't be avoided, but I wish we could've been given more time there. We were able to stroll the grounds on our own and see what we wanted to see, which was nice. Some people chose to shop in the town and get a bite to eat, instead of touring the castle.

We had around 50-60 people on our tour, which made leaving one place and going to another a nightmare. We were always about 20 minutes later leaving than our guide had told us. I will NOT do a big tour again like this, due to this issue.

Stonehenge was great, but they tried to force us onto the shuttle to the site before going to the exhibit. We chose to do the exhibit first, which was a better idea, I thought. We were able to explore the main ruins at Stonehenge, but I would definitely go back to explore the entire site. Again, people were late to the bus and so we were late getting to our next destination.
